==English== ===Etymology=== From {{inh|en|enm|mistaken}}, from {{der|en|non|mistaka|t=to take in error, to miscarry}}; equivalent to {{prefix|en|mis|take}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|mistaka|t=to mistake}}, {{cog|sv|missta|t=to mistake}} (before apocope {{m|sv|misstaga}}). The noun, which replaced earlier {{m|en|mistaking}}, is derived from the verb. Compare {{cog|sv|misstag|t=mistake|pos=noun}}, {{cog|fo|mistak|t=mitake|pos=noun}}, {{cog|is|mistak|t=mistake|pos=noun}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/mɪˈsteɪk/}} ** {{IPA|en|[mɪˈsteɪk]|a=US,RP}} ** {{IPA|en|[mɪˈstɛjk]|a=SSB}} ** {{IPA|en|[mɪˈsteːk]|a=CA}} ** {{IPA|en|[mɪˈstæɪk]|a=AU}} * {{audio|en|en-us-mistake.ogg|a=GA}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪk|s=2}} ===Verb=== {{en-verb|~s|mistaking|mistook|~n}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[understand]] [[wrongly]], taking one thing or person for another. #: {{ux|en|Sorry, I '''mistook''' you for my brother. You look very similar.}} #: {{ux|en|Don't '''mistake''' my kindness for weakness.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|act=IV,|scene=ii|passage=My father’s purposes have been '''mistook''';}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1777|author=w:Samuel Johnson|chapter=Life of the Author|title=The Works of {{w|Richard Savage (poet)|Richard Savage}} with an Account of the Life and Writings of the Author|location=London|publisher=T. Evans|volume=I|page=lxi|url=https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/000780477 |passage=The reigning error of his life was, that he '''mistook''' the love for the practice of virtue, and was indeed not so much a good man, as the friend of goodness.}} #* {{quote-song|en|year=2003|artist={{w|A Perfect Circle|A Perfect Circle }}|title={{w|Blue (A Perfect Circle song)|Blue}}|passage=Because I don't want to know
I didn't want to know
I just didn't want to know
I just didn't want
'''Mistook''' the nods for an approval
Just ignore the smoke and smile}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[misunderstand]] (someone). #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Richard 2|act=II|scene=iii|page=32|passage='''Miſtake''' me not, my Lord, ’tis not my meaning / To raze one Title of your Honour out.}} #* {{RQ:Fielding Tom Jones|volume=I|book=3|chapter=6|page=194|passage={{...}} at last she so evidently demonstrated her Affection to him to be much stronger than what she bore her own Son, that it was impossible to '''mistake''' her any longer.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To commit an unintentional [[error]]; to do or think something wrong. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Much Ado About Nothing|act=V|scene=i|page=119|passage=Impoſe me to what penance your inuention / Can lay vpon my ſinne, yet ſinn’d I not / But in '''miſtaking'''.}} #* '''1720''', {{w|Jonathan Swift}}, “Letter to a Young Clergyman” in ''The Works of Jonathan Swift'', London: Charles Elliot, 1784, Volume 10, pp. 6-7,[https://catalog.hathitrust.org/Record/008661469] #*: No gentleman thinks it is safe or prudent to send a servant with a message, without repeating it more than once, and endeavouring to put it into terms brought down to the capacity of the bearer; yet, after all this care, it is frequent for servants to '''mistake''', and sometimes occasion misunderstandings among friends {{...}} #* {{RQ:Bulwer-Lytton Pelham|volume=I|page=127|chapter=XVI|passage="Bah!" said the Englishwoman: "what knight ever feared cold? Besides, you '''mistake'''; the night is warm, and you look so handsome in your gown."}} #* {{quote-book|en|author=T[héodore] Robertson|chapter=[Charles Saville:{{nb...|Texte complémentaire — racines — mots usuels — idiotismes / combinaison des particules adverbiales avec les verbes / locutions familières et popularies [Additional text — roots — common words — idioms / combination of adverbial particles with verbs / colloquial and popular phrases]}}] Chapter XXV|title=Synthèse de la langue anglaise (Charles Saville) : Texte anglais avec la traduction française en regard|trans-title=Synthesis of the English Language (Charles Saville): English Text with Opposite French Translation|edition=2nd|location=Paris|publisher=Librairie française et anglaise de [French and English bookshop of] J.-H. Truchy; Ch. Leroy, successeur [successor];{{nb...|26, Boulevard des Iitaliens, 26}}|year=1857|page=240|passage=There is also a chancellor, — no, I '''mistake''', — a chandler and green-grocer, with his hands full of warts; {{...}}}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|rare}} To take or choose wrongly. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare King John|act=III|scene=i|page=10|passage=The better act of purposes '''mistook''' / Is to '''mistake''' again; though indirect, / Yet indirection thereby grows direct,}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1716|translator=w:Alexander Pope|title=The {{w|Iliad}} of {{w|Homer}}|location=London|publisher=Bernard Lintott|section=Volume 2, Book 8, lines 151-152, p. 252|url=http://name.umdl.umich.edu/004836009.0001.002 |passage=The Spear with erring Haste '''mistook''' its way,
